speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please describe the onset of these symptoms and exactly where the skin lesions are located. To better assess the severity, have you noticed any joint swelling, redness, or difficulty moving your wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the history of a self-resolving knee pain, could you describe the appearance of the skin lesions on your wrist and whether they are itchy or painful? Additionally, have you noticed any target-like shapes or blisters?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Multiforme (likely triggered by Chlamydia pneumoniae given the history of "knee pain" which may have been reactive arthritis or the infection itself, though the Minnesota camping trip raises suspicion for Lyme disease or other arthropod-borne illnesses). The description of "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" and "target-like shapes" (implied by the doctor's previous question and typical EM presentation) alongside joint pain and fever is classic for Erythema Multiforme. The doctor's prior suggestion of iron deficiency anemia is clinically inconsistent with this acute inflammatory presentation.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Ferritin, CRP, RPR/VDRL, and Lyme_Serology.
